Save a plot at its final journal size

Source: R/export.R
save_olinkviz.Rd

Exports a ggplot, patchwork, or pheatmap object at an exact physical size in one or more formats. PDFs use the Cairo device so fonts are embedded; PNG, SVG and TIFF use `ggplot2::ggsave()` defaults (ragg or svglite when installed). Typical widths are 89 mm (single column) and 183 mm (double column), but check the journal's author guidelines.

Usage

save_olinkviz(
  plot,
  file,
  width = 89,
  height = 70,
  units = "mm",
  formats = c("pdf", "png"),
  dpi = 300
)

Arguments

plot

A `ggplot`, `patchwork`, `pheatmap`, or `gtable`/`grob` object, e.g. the result of any `plot_*()` function. For base-graphics plots ([plot_corr()]) open a device yourself (for example `grDevices::cairo_pdf()`), call the function, and close the device.

file

Output path. A file extension is ignored; one file per entry of `formats` is written next to it.

width, height

Size of the figure in `units`.

units

`"mm"` (default), `"cm"` or `"in"`.

formats

Any of `"pdf"`, `"png"`, `"svg"`, `"tiff"`. Default `c("pdf", "png")`.

dpi

Resolution of raster formats (default 300).

Value

Invisibly, the paths of the files written.

Examples

# \donttest{
old <- olinkviz_options(base_size = 7)
p <- plot_boxplot(probc, assay = "IL6", group = "Project")
save_olinkviz(p, file.path(tempdir(), "il6_boxplot"), width = 89, height = 70)
options(old)
# }
